We Gave Five AI Video Generators the Same Prompt: Which Produced the Most Usable Video?

AI video generators can turn text prompts into short videos, but their results vary in realism, motion, consistency, and usability. We explore five popular tools and a practical testing method to determine which produces the most useful video for content creators, marketers, and beginners

By LokkeeVerse · 11 min read

Creating professional-looking videos used to require a camera, editing software, and hours of work. Today, AI video generators can transform written descriptions into video clips, making it possible to experiment with visual storytelling without filming every scene yourself.

A creator can describe a futuristic city, a product advertisement, or a cinematic scene and let an AI model generate a video based on the prompt.

However, not every generated video is good enough to publish. Some tools produce impressive visuals but struggle with movement. Others generate realistic scenes but introduce strange details, inconsistent objects, or unwanted changes between frames.

For content creators, the important question is not simply which AI video generator creates the most impressive demonstration. It is which tool produces footage that can actually be used in a real project.

In this comparison, we examine five AI video generators and establish a practical method for testing them with the same prompt. The goal is to help creators identify the differences that matter when choosing a tool for social media videos, advertisements, storytelling, and other creative projects.

This article is a comparison framework, not a report of a completed hands-on benchmark. No actual generation results or performance rankings are claimed without verified test evidence.

The Experiment: One Prompt for All Five Tools

A fair comparison requires the same creative brief, similar output settings, and a consistent evaluation method.

For this experiment, the objective is to generate a short product advertisement featuring a smartphone on a desk.

The scene is deliberately simple enough to reproduce across different tools but detailed enough to reveal problems with motion, lighting, object consistency, and prompt interpretation.

The Test Prompt

Use the following prompt in each tool that supports text-to-video generation:

"Create an 8-second photorealistic product advertisement featuring a premium black smartphone standing upright on a clean dark desk in a modern studio. Soft blue and light-blue lighting illuminates the phone, with subtle reflections on the desk. The camera slowly moves from left to right while the phone remains stationary. The screen displays an abstract blue gradient with no text or logos. The background is minimal, elegant, and uncluttered. Use realistic materials, smooth camera movement, consistent proportions, and professional commercial lighting. No people, no extra phones, no distorted objects, and no visible text."

The prompt specifies a subject, environment, lighting, camera movement, and restrictions. These details make it easier to identify differences between the outputs.

Why Use the Same Prompt?

If every generator receives a different description, the comparison becomes unreliable. A more detailed prompt for one tool could produce a better result simply because it provides more instructions.

Using identical wording gives the tools a shared starting point.

Nevertheless, the models may interpret prompts differently, and their available duration, aspect ratio, resolution, or motion settings may not match exactly. Any differences should be recorded rather than ignored.

If a tool cannot generate an eight-second clip, use its closest supported duration and document the limitation.

How to Evaluate the Results

A video should not win simply because it looks impressive in a single frame. The entire clip must be evaluated.

1. Visual Quality

Examine the sharpness of the image, lighting, composition, textures, and realism of the smartphone.

Look for distorted edges, inconsistent reflections, strange shadows, or details that change unexpectedly between frames.

A high-quality result should look suitable for the intended project without requiring extensive repairs.

2. Motion Quality

The prompt asks for a slow camera movement while the smartphone remains stationary.

Check whether the camera moves smoothly and whether the phone maintains its shape and position.

Watch for sudden jumps, unwanted object movement, flickering, and changes in the background that make the scene look artificial.

3. Prompt Accuracy

The generated video should follow the instructions.

Evaluate whether the output contains the requested black smartphone, dark desk, blue lighting, clean background, and camera movement.

Extra objects, unwanted text, incorrect colours, or a moving phone would count against the result.

4. Consistency

An AI-generated video may look convincing at the beginning but become distorted as the clip progresses.

Check whether the phone's dimensions, screen, edges, and reflections remain reasonably consistent throughout the video.

Consistency is especially important for advertisements, where product appearance needs to remain recognizable.

5. Usability

Ask whether the video could be used in an actual project.

A clip may have attractive visuals but still be unsuitable if the product is distorted, the movement is distracting, or the scene does not match the intended advertisement.

Consider whether the output could be published as it is or would require substantial editing.

6. Generation Cost and Accessibility

Record how many attempts were needed to produce a satisfactory clip, whether the tool required a paid plan, and whether watermarks or export restrictions affected the result.

A generator that creates a good video after one attempt may be more practical than one that requires several generations.

Free access should be verified at the time of testing. A free account may have limited credits, restricted resolution, queues, or other limitations.

The Scoring System

To make the comparison easier to understand, assign each category a score from one to five.

  • Visual quality: 1–5 points.
  • Motion quality: 1–5 points.
  • Prompt accuracy: 1–5 points.
  • Consistency: 1–5 points.
  • Usability: 1–5 points.

This produces a maximum score of 25 points per generator.

The total score is a useful summary, but the individual category scores should also be published. A tool that produces excellent visuals but poor motion may still be useful for certain projects.

For a stronger evaluation, generate at least three clips per tool under the same conditions. Record every attempt, then report both the average score and the best result.

This reduces the risk of declaring a winner based on one unusually good or bad generation.

Which Tool Is Best for Different Creators?

There may not be one universal winner. The most suitable generator depends on what you want to create.

For Product Advertisements

Prioritize accurate products, consistent details, clean lighting, and predictable camera movement.

A beautiful video is not enough if the product changes shape or develops features that do not exist.

For Faceless YouTube Videos

Consider scene quality, the ability to generate relevant footage, visual consistency, and how easily the clips fit into an editing workflow.

Also consider licensing terms, the amount of editing required, and whether the generated footage supports the story being told.

For TikTok and Instagram Reels

Short-form creators may prioritize fast experimentation, portrait-friendly output, visual impact, and manageable generation costs.

The best tool is the one that can consistently produce footage suitable for the creator's format and audience.

For Cinematic Storytelling

Look closely at camera movement, atmosphere, lighting, scene continuity, and character consistency.

A visually impressive clip may still be difficult to use in a longer story if the characters or environment change unexpectedly between generations.

Can AI Video Generators Replace Traditional Video Production?

AI video generators can reduce the need to film certain scenes, especially when creating conceptual visuals, atmospheric footage, animated sequences, or early advertising concepts.

They can also help creators who lack access to professional cameras, studios, or locations.

However, AI-generated footage still has limitations. It may introduce visual errors, struggle with precise actions, or fail to reproduce the same character or product consistently across multiple shots.

Traditional production also provides direct control over real people, physical products, timing, and specific actions.

For many creators, the most practical approach is a combination of AI-generated footage, traditional editing, and human review.

Important Limitations of This Comparison

The quality of AI-generated video changes as models and services are updated. A comparison conducted today may produce different results after a model update.

Access may also vary by country, subscription, and account type. Some services may impose generation limits or restrict certain features to paid users.

Finally, a text-to-video test does not measure every capability. Image-to-video generation, character references, editing features, audio generation, and scene extension may produce different results.

The conclusions should therefore be limited to the prompts, settings, models, and dates actually tested.

Final Verdict

AI video generation is becoming a useful option for content creators, marketers, and businesses that need visual content without filming every scene themselves.

Runway, Kling AI, Google Veo, Luma Dream Machine, and Pika are five candidates worth evaluating, but naming an overall winner requires evidence from comparable generations.

A fair test should use the same prompt, document any differences in settings, inspect the full clips, and evaluate visual quality, motion, accuracy, consistency, cost, and practical usability.

For ToolPillot readers, the most useful result would be a transparent comparison containing the actual generated videos, screenshots, scores, and observations.

That evidence would help readers choose a generator based on their own needs instead of relying on promotional demonstrations or unsupported rankings.

Ultimately, the best AI video generator is not necessarily the one that creates the most spectacular clip. It is the one that produces footage you can reliably use for your project at a cost and quality level that makes sense.
